mandate.target: the open-issue backlog is trustworthy AND vision-aligned -- every fleet:claimed label has a live matching PR, every open issue is real current work, and nothing open contradicts or ignores the target repo's own stated north star
checklist: PART 0 -- read the vision from the TARGET repo, not from fleet-kit: cat FLEET_REPO/CLAUDE.md (and AGENTS.md if present) and find its north-star/vision section -- this repo changes independently of fleet-kit, so re-read it fresh every pass, never cache or assume last pass's vision still holds
PART A -- claim hygiene: list every open issue labeled fleet:claimed
for each, check for an open PR that actually references/fixes it
no matching open PR -> stale claim (a builder pass died mid-work, or claimed and never started) -- remove fleet:claimed, comment once saying why
a matching open PR exists -> leave the label alone, it is correct
PART B -- cruft prune: walk the rest of the open backlog (not just fleet:claimed ones)

an issue is cruft if: a merged/closed PR already fixed it, it duplicates another still-open issue, the thing it describes no longer exists in the repo (renamed/deleted file, retired feature), or it's been superseded by a newer issue on the same topic -- verify each with a real check (gh pr list --search, grep the repo, read the newer issue), never close on a hunch
confirmed cruft -> gh issue close <n> --reason "not planned" --comment "marie: closing as cruft -- <one-line evidence: which PR/commit/newer issue fixed or superseded this>"
genuinely still-relevant work, even if old or vague -> leave it open, do not touch
never close or edit the issue body itself -- labels + close + comment only, body is the author's record
never close two issues into each other in a loop -- if A and B both claim to supersede the other, leave both open and flag the conflict in your report
mandate.escalation: can't tell if a PR/claim is stale vs genuinely still in progress, or can't find hard evidence an issue is cruft -- leave it alone and say so in the report rather than guessing wrong. A false stale-clear or false close is worse than a missed one: one lets two builders claim the same item, the other silently deletes real signal a human hasn't seen yet.
